Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
928 PM EDT Thu Sep 3 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A new Severe T-storm Watch has been issued for most of the area
outside of locations along and south of US-33 until 2ma Friday. A
Severe T-Storm Watch remains for portions of western MD and the
eastern WV until midnight. Monitoring a a large cluster of
storms dropping south and east along the PA/MD border from
Hagerstown, MD west to Morgantown/Wheeling, WV. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Hot temperatures, high humidity, and severe thunderstorm 
chances look to continue through Friday. 

- 2) Mostly dry conditions and lowering humidity for the Labor Day 
holiday weekend ahead.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Heat, humidity, and severe thunderstorm chances look 
to continue through Friday. 

The Severe T-Storm Watch has been expanded further east of the
Alleghenies and north of US-33 through 2am Friday. For western
MD and the eastern WV Panhandle the Severe T-Storm Watch remains
until midnight. Damaging winds, large hail, and locally heavy 
rainfall will be the primary threat with these storms as they 
push south from the PA/MD border and north-central WV between 
10PM-2am. Further watch expansion may be needed on the southern
end if storms survive. 

Overall monitoring a clusters of storms (MCS) dropping souyth
from Morgantown/Wheeling, wv to Cumberland/Hagerstown, MD. This
storm complex will have plenty of instability to work with 
given pooling CAPE values of 3000-5000 j/kg. Locally, mid- level
lapse rates of 6.5-7 C/km (per latest mesoanalysis and the KIAD
00Z RAOB) atop a very moist boundary layer with surface dew 
points well into the 70s F will lead to increasing CAPE despite 
the late start at surface heating. The question then becomes 
just how organized upstream storms become, and how stable the 
boundary layer is heading further into the evening. A more 
organized and potent line of storms a bit earlier in the evening
would result in a notably higher risk for more numerous 
damaging wind gusts, especially focused along the residual 
baroclinic zone/theta-e gradient which should lie near the 
Potomac River/US- 50/I-66 this evening. A somewhat slower and/or
more disorganized line would result in a lower risk for severe 
surface gusts, though some isolated damaging winds would still 
be possible given high CAPE/DCAPE and the shallow nature of the 
stable layer near the surface. Areas of western Maryland and 
perhaps into the eastern West Virginia panhandle are most likely
to see the storms prior to the onset of appreciable nocturnal 
boundary layer stability.

The area remains in a Slight Risk (level 2 out of 5) for severe 
weather from SPC as of the 20z/4pm outlook update, driven mostly by 
the threat of damaging wind gusts. There is a threat for large hail 
in stronger cores, though mid-level lapse rates will gradually 
become less steep tonight. A linear storm mode would tend to be less 
favorable for large hail production (as opposed to 
discrete/individual cells), as well. A few discrete cells are 
possible this evening in weak low-level WAA, however, independent of 
any linear system that may affect the region. These storms would be 
most likely to develop over northern and central Virginia into 
central Maryland along a weak surface trough and the aforementioned 
moisture/instability gradient.

Current timing has this initial round of storms into western MD and 
eastern WV between 7-9pm gradually advancing east toward 
northern and central MD and northern VA between 9pm-midnight. 
The secondary complex of storms will push south and east mostly 
likely after 10pm- 2am. Pending how much energy the first 
complex of storms zaps away combined with the nocturnal stable 
layer will determine how of the secondary complex survives. The
severity may drop off although gusty winds, frequent lightning,
and locally heavy rainfall will remain the primary concerns. 

Additional showers and thunderstorms, possibly strong to severe, are 
anticipated again on Friday. Timing is a bit uncertain given the 
subtle waves aloft, but increasing low-level convergence paired with 
another upper impulse may very well result in another round or two 
of storms with a damaging wind risk. The latest guidance has nudged 
the threat a bit further north, encompassing areas as far north as I-
70 or the Mason-Dixon line (as opposed to I-66/US-50). This will 
depend on any residual early day clouds or convection, of course.

Lows tonight will fall into the upper 60s and mid 70s with heat 
index values in the mid 70s and low 80s. Highs Friday will 
range from the upper 80s to lower 90s with dew points in the 
lower to middle 70s resulting in heat indices in the upper 90s 
to lower 100s. This will be just shy of heat headline criteria 
(except in Charlottesville and surrounding Albemarle/Nelson 
Counties). The potential for early day clouds to offset heating 
precludes enough confidence to issue any further heat headlines 
at this time, though it will be unusually hot and humid for 
early September regardless.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Drier conditions expected for the Labor Day weekend 
through early next week.

A high pressure system over the Great Lakes continues to track 
southeastward towards our forecast region through Tuesday. Over this 
time period, condtions remain predominantly dry, apart from 
 an isolated shower in the Appalachian mountains. 

Temperatures remain seasonable for early September this weekend, 
with temperatures rising above normal by Tuesday. Moist and warmer 
conditions return as we head into the middle of next week. Warm, 
moist air at the surface could lead to unstable conditions, with 
chances for showers and thunderstorms returning by late Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /01Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
VFR conditions look to prevail through at least 23z/7pm for most of 
the corridor. Watching a complex of storms up around KPIT that 
looks to dive into areas west of MRB/HGR between 00-02z/7-10pm.
This activity will gradually sags south and east toward the 
rest of the corridor beyond 00-03z/8-11pm. Utilized PROB30s 
between 01-06z/9pm-2am to encompass this threat as the complex 
of storms drops south and east from southwest PA. Gusty winds 
and frequent lightning will be the primary threat with any 
storms that develop. Some uncertainty remains in regards to the 
severity of storms as they push to the eastern end of the 
corridor and down toward KCHO/KSHD. 

Winds will vary between W and SW as a surface trough develops 
overhead with speeds generally AOB 10 kts. Guidance is not keen on 
low clouds or fog overnight into early Friday, though the pattern 
would suggest at least some conditional potential.

Additional storms with somewhat uncertain timing are possible 
Friday. Was too low on confidence in timing for 18Z TAFs, but 
PROB30s are likely to be included in subsequent updates, focused 
probably on the typical peak diurnal window (~19Z-01Z). Winds will 
shift to NW by late Friday through Saturday.

This weekend into early next week, prevailing VFR conditions are 
expected across all terminals. Light northeasterly winds on Sunday 
shift easterly by Monday.

&&

.MARINE...
Special Marine Warnings may be needed this evening as storms
develop and track towards the waters. Additional storms are
anticipated on Friday, most likely late afternoon and evening.
Otherwise, generally light flow is expected into the upcoming
weekend, though NW gusts could approach SCA levels Friday night
into Saturday.

On Sunday and Monday, wind gusts remain below SCA-criteria with 
highest chances for approaching SCA thresholds Sunday afternoon or 
evening. Light northeasterly winds on Sunday shift easterly by 
Monday.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...DHOF/EST/KVH
AVIATION...DHOF/EST/KVH
MARINE...DHOF/KVH
